correctness.rationale: For p=2 direct values beta(3)=2,beta(4)=3,beta(5)=4 rule out both neighbors. For p odd, beta(2p)=p−1 and m=2p+epsilon imply 2 beta(m)=m−c, c=epsilon+2 in {1,3}. Exhaustive factorization for odd m with Omega(m)<=3: prime, square, cube, qr, q^2r are excluded by the displayed exact identities/positivity; qrs with q>=5 or q=3,r>=7 is excluded by the multiplicative ratio bounds >1. Thus q=3,r=5 and 16(s−1)=15s−c, whence s=16−c: only c=3 yields prime s=13, m=195 and p=97. Independent factorization check for all primes p<10000 returned only (97,195), beta(194)=beta(195)=96. The six-case analytic exhaustion, not finite search, proves all primes.
